limits: No matched comparison with direct Codex, no measured superiority, no full overnight soak or months-long reliability claim.
Planning, qualitative assessment and project review use the same Codex integration; they are not independent certification.
The real SDK fault is deliberately injected after a successful model response. Its initial task is a fixture. The actual C2 product activity and graph note are separate real model-planned work.
The graph error/replay/keyboard audit uses explicit deterministic fixtures and no model; it covers selected keyboard paths, not complete accessibility or arbitrary-client idempotency.
Only returned semantic Compass orientation failures are corrected automatically. Provider, authentication, timeout, permission, integrity and protected-path failures remain blocking.

The first mission needed four assistant interventions, including an explicit tested supervisor upgrade. B had no during-run steering. C2 had one intentional graph instruction. The stopped C1 attempt and its setup conflict remain recorded.
Dependencies for this known repository were prepared privately; arbitrary repository environment provisioning and a live remote SSH host were not tested.
Final wire projections of four actual histories were compared; every prefix was checked only for the separate frozen 40-prefix legacy fixture.
Unsent drafts are page-local. A completed technical run does not automatically mark the product milestone reviewed.
This documentation-only delivery changes the whole-tree fingerprint. Historical acceptance remains attributed to its preserved original run worktree, not silently transferred to a new run.
